description: Lobster is a Openclaw-native workflow shell: a typed, local-first “macro engine” that turns skills/tools into composable pipelines and safe automations—and lets Openclaw call those workflows in one step.

summary.one_liner: Lobster is an OpenClaw-native, typed, local-first workflow shell that chains shell commands, data-shaping stages, LLM calls and approval gates into reusable pipelines and YAML workflow files.
summary.what_it_does: Lobster runs pipelines of typed (JSON-first) stages such as exec, where, pick, head, json and table, passing objects and arrays between them rather than text. Workflow files (.lobster, YAML or JSON) define steps using run/command for shell, pipeline for native stages, and approval for human gates, with stdin data passing between steps via $step.stdout or $step.json. A graph command renders workflow structure as Mermaid, DOT or ASCII. Built-in stages include llm.invoke (OpenClaw, pi or HTTP providers), openclaw.agent, and openclaw.invoke/clawd.invoke shims for calling OpenClaw tools. It also provides retry, timeout and on_error policies per step, cost tracking with cost limits for LLM usage, resumable approvals and input requests, and an SDK with AbortSignal cancellation. Example recipes include a GitHub PR monitor that notifies only when a pull request changes.
use_cases: chain shell commands into typed data pipelines
add human approval gates to automated workflows
call OpenClaw tools or agents from a single workflow step
monitor a GitHub pull request for changes
run LLM steps with cost limits inside scripted workflows
visualize workflow structure as a diagram before running it
notable: Typed JSON-first pipelines instead of text pipes
Approval and input gates that pause a workflow and resume with the user's decision
Workflow graph visualization in Mermaid, DOT and ASCII
Cost tracking and cost_limit for LLM calls, with replay-aware billing
Output and HTTP response byte limits via environment variables
caveats: Requires Node.js 22 or newer and the pinned pnpm version; the README says to build after changing source because bin/lobster.js runs compiled dist output.
Retries are suppressed after an OpenClaw dispatch is attempted, so failed remote calls must be checked manually before rerunning.
The OpenClaw llm-task adapter does not return token usage, so token-based cost limits cannot be enforced for those calls.
